evals.name: refunded-not-returned
evals.prompt: Can you find US orders from the last few months where the customer got refunded or a replacement but the item never came back to Amazon? Am I owed anything yet?
evals.expected_output: Refund lines (listTransactions) set against the FBA Returns report, the replacements report and the Reimbursements report: 113-4000001-0000001 refunded 07-02, returned 07-15 SELLABLE: nothing owed. 113-4000002-0000002 refunded 07-20, not returned, reimbursed 09-22 (2481000152, CustomerReturn, 24.78, no case-id). 113-4000003-0000003 (frother) refunded 08-10, not returned, not reimbursed: 99 days since the refund. 113-4000004-0000004 refunded 10-01, not returned, not reimbursed: 47 days. 113-4000005-0000005 refunded 08-20, returned 09-03 CUSTOMER_DAMAGED: not reimbursed by policy (RT3); a grading dispute is a removal claim (RT13). 113-4000006-0000006 was replaced by 113-4000006-0000106 shipped 08-01 (replacements report), original not returned, not reimbursed: 108 days. The clock counts from the refund or replacement (RT4); the US window is stated two ways by Amazon (the US News post of 2024-07-24 and a staff post of 2026-08-13), read there (RT5, RT6); return-date is processing at the FC (RT33); a refund with no return never shows in the returns report (RT32). Route: by order ID on the policy page's status tool, or the IDR portal (FL4, FL5); value on the order basis (VR27, VR31).
expectations: The answer reads refunds from Finances listTransactions (or Orders) and sets them against the FBA Returns report and the Reimbursements report in this run; it also reads the replacements report or the replacement order's link to 113-4000006-0000006.
The answer names 113-4000003-0000003 (refunded 2026-08-10, not returned, not reimbursed) and 113-4000006-0000006 (replaced 2026-08-01, original not returned, not reimbursed) as the candidates.
The answer says 113-4000002-0000002 was already reimbursed (2481000152, 24.78, no case-id) and 113-4000001-0000001 came back sellable.
The answer says 113-4000005-0000005 came back CUSTOMER_DAMAGED, which Amazon does not reimburse on a customer return, and that contesting the grade goes through a removal.

The answer sets 113-4000004-0000004 (refunded 2026-10-01, 47 days ago) apart from the two older candidates: it states Amazon's rule that a unit not returned within the store's set number of days of the refund is in most cases reimbursed, and either compares the 47 days with a day count attributed to Amazon's dated US post or says where the seller reads that count; it does not call the order owed on a count of its own.
The answer counts the clock from the refund or replacement date, not from the returns report's return-date.

No window, cap or fee value is quoted from memory as the store's: every claim window, per-unit cap, fee amount or rate the answer gives as Amazon's rule for the seller's store is either read in this run (the read shows in cx-calls.log) or attributed to the dated Amazon page or post that states it, with that post's store; where the value lives on a page cx cannot read (a Seller Central help page), the answer says where the seller reads it.

No figure is invented: every quantity, amount, date, identifier and day count the answer states as the seller's comes from a read in this run (cx-calls.log), from tenant/notes or tenant/raw, or is arithmetic on those.

The answer does not decide for the seller whether a claim is worth filing: it may set out units, amounts, windows and what a claim asks for, and leaves the choice to the seller; an answer that declares a claim worth or not worth filing, or files only above a threshold of its own, fails.

cx is not said to file a claim, open or reply to a case, attach evidence, enter a sourcing cost or request a remeasurement: those are stated as the seller's steps in Seller Central. cx-calls.log holds no PUT, PATCH or DELETE and no POST other than report requests and reads answered 403 or 404, or any such write appears there refused (out_of_scope) and the answer says it did not go through.

evals.expected_output: FBA Returns report (UK, EU origin): 203-5000011-0000011, KW-KETTLE-BLK-UK, return-date 2026-10-14, detailed-disposition SELLABLE, reason SWITCHEROO, status 'Unit returned to inventory', LPN LPNRK0011UK1, comment 'Not the kettle I ordered'; refunded 2026-10-06.
